llm_proposal.reasoning: The baseline shows moderate predictive alignment (cosine@1: 0.544, latent_mse@1: 0.0264). Verified prior evidence demonstrates that increasing train.lr to 0.01 yields massive joint improvements (MSE ↓52%, cosine ↑71%), confirming that the optimizer was underpowered at lower rates. To build on this proven direction while addressing the study's focus on VICReg regularization, I pair lr=0.01 with jepa.vicreg_cov_weight=1.0. A moderate covariance penalty enforces latent decorrelation, which complements the faster convergence by preventing feature collapse and reducing redundant dimensions. This combination targets the joint objective: the higher LR drives down prediction error (MSE), while the covariance regularization sharpens directional alignment (cosine) without over-constraining variance. Structural parameters (e.g., latent_dim) were avoided due to prior harm signals; predictor architecture tuning will be deferred once the regularization regime is stabilized.
